title: Seams & Tangles Review (periodical run 6): area knots, dependency direction, ways in, rebuild readiness and change coupling — delta vs the 2026-11-04 run (8-commit window; the records-first cost-read cutover and the first guide edit since run 4)
description:
<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="seams-tangles" -->

**Periodical: Seams & Tangles (corrective, run 6, delta against the 2026-11-04 run).** Read how Harbour's **areas** depend on each other: where they knot, which way they point, whether each has a clear way in, how ready each is to be refactored or rebuilt behind a seam, and which areas keep **changing together**. Write a trend-framed, severity-ranked report, get an adversarial second-read, merge the report PR, mint at most \~3 one-move follow-ups, then conclude this task. **Review-only:** no code, config, guide (`scripts/code-shape/areas.json`) or doc edits beyond the report and its evidence files.

This run is also read as the **top-down reading for the Survey research** (`docs/plans/survey/log.md` and `docs/plans/survey/place-ledger.md` on branch `claude/cool-rubin-6acj5j`). That is context for what the numbers are used for, not extra scope: do not edit anything on that branch, and do not change what you report to fit it. If a finding bears on a place named in the place ledger, say so in one line and cross-link; the Survey's own docs are not this review's to change.

## Grounding (as found at mint time, `origin/main` = `d7ceb373444f9efbc027656132352d247535aa5e`, 2026-11-04 17:18Z). Re-verify all of it; nothing here is a finding.

* **Repo:** `JKershaw/LinearViewer` (Harbour). PR and commit convention: `LIN-NNNN: <summary> (#PR)`. `ci-success` must be green before merging (`CLAUDE.md`).
* **Report convention:** `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-YYYY-MM-DD.md`, with raw tool JSON and guide copies in `docs/reviews/_evidence-YYYY-MM-DD/`. Today's date is the same as run 5's (2026-11-04), so **pick a distinct name** (for example `seams-tangles-review-2026-11-04-run6.md` and `_evidence-2026-11-04-run6/`) and do not overwrite run 5's files. `lib/periodical-report-gate.js` needs a comment on this task that cites a GitHub commit, PR or blob URL, plus the three second-read fields in one comment body, before Done.
* **Prior run (the baseline):** `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-2026-11-04.md` (run 5, LIN-4208, Done, PR #2268, merge `e439f6374def25f76cdcdf6941e0446920fc627a`). It measured `5334c81a7207b9f2cc85ca429a2c6b18e1635c0e`. Read §0 (what was measured), §1 (changes), §2 (the four-run table and the guide effect), §3 (findings F1 to F8 and N1 to N8, with N6 `lib/cost-read.js` ranked first), §6 (change coupling), §7 (guide proposals P1, P1b, P2, P3), §8 (existing tickets), §9 (no follow-ups minted, and why), §10 (second-read: DISAGREE, fixed in place) and §11 (the ledger with its stable names). Run 4 (`seams-tangles-review-2026-11-03.md`) is background.
* **This is a thin window, not a busy one.** `5334c81a..d7ceb373` is **8 commits over about 12 hours** (2026-11-04 05:23Z to 17:18Z). Four are docs-only review reports (`e439f637` this series' run 5, `1403d52d` Code Quality, `57b22b92` Stability, `f5bc752c` Drift & Coherence). Four are code: LIN-4200 (`230cc2c2`, measurement scripts), LIN-4212 (`eb44eff9`), LIN-4201 (`2ee4e600`, the records-first cost-read cutover, LIN-4195 piece 4) and LIN-4203 (`d7ceb373`, the runner kit stops posting `[usage]`). Production (`lib routes public server.js`) is **33 files, +1,049 / -288** (verify with `git diff --shortstat 5334c81a d7ceb373 -- lib routes public server.js`). **Added:** `lib/request-usage-fold.js`, `lib/request-usage-loader.js`, `lib/request-usage-vocabulary.js`, `lib/usage-snapshot-intake.js`, `lib/workspace-kpis-cache.js`. **Deleted:** `lib/founder-lookup.js`. **A short, mostly-unchanged report is a genuine outcome here: do not pad it to match run 5's size.** The honest work is the delta on what moved (the cost read, the guide edit, the five new files), and the carried-forward open items.
* **The guide changed in the window, which is new since run 5.** `scripts/code-shape/areas.json` was edited by LIN-4201 (`2ee4e600`): `cost-read`, `row-usage` and `lineage-membership` were added to the "Runs & dispatch" pattern, and `workspace-kpis-cache` to "Reports & operator tools". The tools did not change (last touched by LIN-3881, `856d8ae6`, 2026-10-25). **Run both guides (**`5334c81a`**'s and HEAD's) at both commits** and record the guide effect apart from code movement; a difference must be separable into placement and code. Quote `"${SHA}:scripts/code-shape/areas.json"` in `git show` (bare `$SHA:s…` is a zsh modifier and silently yields the wrong file). `seams.mjs` needs `acorn`: run it from a tree that has `node_modules`.
* **What a quick mint-time pass saw (verify, don't quote):**
  * Files in scope (seams, `scope.files`): **536 -> 540**, 0 parse failures, 0 non-literal dynamic imports, 0 unmapped files, **4 unresolved relative imports** (as run 5: `routes/test.js`). `lib/` -> `routes/` imports: 0 by `git grep` at HEAD.
  * Knot pairs 12 -> 12; one knot group of 9 areas -> 9. Cross-area link total on the HEAD guide **1,249 -> 1,259** (this is the HEAD guide at both commits; run 5's 1,262 was the *old* guide at `5334c81a`, so do not compare across guides). On the **old guide** at HEAD the total is 1,275.
  * **The "Other features" catch-all: run 5 reported 17 files (old guide at** `5334c81a`**). Under the HEAD guide it is 14 at both commits, and under the old guide at HEAD it is 17.** The guide edit placed three catch-all files in Runs: `cost-read` (one of run 5's five new files) and `row-usage` and `lineage-membership` (two of run 4's twelve). Verify the arithmetic (17 - 3, then the deletion of `founder-lookup` and any addition) rather than assume it. So run 5's N6 (`cost-read` as a hub inside the catch-all) and part of N1 changed by **placement**, not code: say how much of the F1 / N6 reading moves with it. `lib/founder-lookup.js` (one of run 5's five new catch-all files) is deleted. `lib/key-state.js`, `lib/key-state-holders.js` and `lib/cost-format.js` should still be catch-all members: check.
  * **F1, LLM & prompts <-> Runs & dispatch**, HEAD guide: **29/36 -> 30/37** (+1/+1). Separate how much is real (new edges into the five new request-usage files, `cost-read`'s records-first rewrite) from placement.
  * New modules to place and read for direction and way-in: `lib/request-usage-fold.js`, `request-usage-loader.js`, `request-usage-vocabulary.js` (Runs by the `request-usage-[^/]*` pattern; check), `lib/usage-snapshot-intake.js` (check which area the guide puts it in, and which routes import it), `lib/workspace-kpis-cache.js` (now Reports).
  * **Change coupling** (`--days 60`, HEAD guide): at `5334c81a` **874 changes, 400 touch 2+ areas, 76 pairs,** `shallow: false`**, 5,273 unmapped files**; at `d7ceb373` **854 / 392 / 76 / 5,351**. The two windows share about 59.5 of 60 days, so expect almost no movement; say plainly that the delta is bounded by that overlap.
  * Run 5's other measurable items, to re-measure rather than assume: `window.X =` in `public/` (run 5: 100) and in `public/common.js` (52); route -> route file edges (53); `proxy-preamble` importers (F4); `tree.js` importers; `task-page-loader.js` cross-area importers; `run-controls.js` (19).
* **Carried open items from run 5 (check each against the code, not ticket state):**
  * **LIN-4154 (FU-1, Backlog, parent LIN-3490):** `fmtDuration` out of `lib/render-run-steps.js`. **LIN-4155 (FU-2, Backlog, parent LIN-3820):** `applyDefaultDispatchHarness` out of `proxy-preamble`. Both have 0 comments and are about half a day old; say whether anything moved.
  * **FU-3 (recorded only):** Providers -> `recommendation-facts` (`parentNextOf`), cross-linked to LIN-3922 and LIN-3923 (both Backlog).
  * **Unparented seam tickets, all Backlog at last check:** LIN-3736, LIN-3737, LIN-3738, LIN-3555, LIN-2600, LIN-3922.
  * **LIN-4193 (Backlog, parent LIN-3936):** name the cost modules into an area and rename `weekly-budget.js`. Run 5 proposed commenting that the whole catch-all is the better-scoped ask. LIN-4201's guide edit has now done part of that for three of the cost files: say what is left for LIN-4193 and whether the comment was posted. LIN-4195 is still In Progress; LIN-4200, LIN-4201 and LIN-4203 are Done.
  * **Guide proposals from run 5:** P1b (place the catch-all), P2 (`tree.js` to Task model; model routing its own area) and P3 (`^experiments/rebuild-[^/]+/` to Reports & operator tools, measured as a labelled experiment in run 5). Say which are now partly adopted by LIN-4201 and which still stand. Nothing here is a guide edit by this review.
  * Run 5 N8 (a stale `task-cost` alias in the Runs pattern at `areas.json:24` and stale comments citing `lib/task-cost.js`): the alias is still in the HEAD guide's Runs pattern (`...|task-cost|terminal-marked-task-cost|...`); check the comments.
  * PR #2185 (LIN-4028, `lib/routing-ruling.js`): last seen open and not on main.
* **Direction rule:** the only written one is that `lib/` never imports `routes/` (LIN-675, `docs/architecture/source-map.md`). Re-confirm 0.
* **Siblings and the seams between them** (read their latest reports' sibling sections for hand-offs): **Drift & Coherence** (`drift-coherence-review-2026-11-04.md`, LIN-4209, Done) owns decisions held in several places, file-level direction, file-level SCCs, text contracts and Simple Dispatcher's cross-repo contract. **Code Quality** (`code-quality-review-2026-11-04.md`, LIN-4207) owns function size. **Stability** (`stability-review-2026-11-04.md`, LIN-4206) owns churn and per-file change counts. Three reviews (Code Quality, Stability, Drift) landed after run 5 measured; read them for hand-offs to this one. **Data & Fetch Architecture**, **API Quality**, **Performance/Scale**, **Comprehension-Debt** (all 2026-10-23) and **Integration & Surface Maturity** (2026-10-21) have not run since. The cost work has its own review `cost-tracking-review-2026-11-02.md` (LIN-4126). **Simple Dispatcher** (`JKershaw/simple-dispatcher`) is flat CommonJS and outside what `seams.mjs` reads; say whether that still holds, and don't build a tool.
* **Parent context:** LIN-3549 (Done, code shape as a standard capability). `docs/runbooks/improvement-cycles.md` reads this report as a standing measure for the find-and-fix round.

## What to do

* **Audit the scope before executing.** Treat the scope above as a starting point to extend, not a checklist to stay inside. Before running the review, look for what is *in-remit but unlisted* (surfaces this review should cover that this scope did not name) and fold them in. Examples to check: files the guide places in the catch-all or by an over-broad regex (anything added since run 5, and `lib/workspace-issues-memo.js` in Auth via `workspace-(?!kpi-stats\.js)[^/]*`); the guide edit itself (LIN-4201) and what it did to run 5's N1 and N6; the records-first cutover's new door and hub shape (`request-usage-fold`, `-loader`, `-vocabulary`, `usage-snapshot-intake`); wiring in `server.js`; the runner kit's change (LIN-4203, `lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs`, a cross-repo-shaped edge outside `seams.mjs`); the browser seam (`public/cost-format.js`, `window.X` globals, `scripts:` lists); in-flight work (LIN-4195, PR #2185). A scope you could only shrink is suspect; the expected move is to widen it to what the remit actually reaches. Stay **broad in discovery but bounded in output**: the wider scope changes *what you examine*, not *what you report*. The report stays uncapped and severity-ranked (a clean, near-empty result is a genuine outcome), and the follow-up bound below stays as it is.
* **Read prior runs first. This review is trend-aware.** Find and read this review's earlier reports (confirm where they are recorded rather than trusting the path above), then frame every knot as a delta against the previous run: new, unchanged, improved, worsened or resolved, never a point-in-time snapshot. Keep run 5's stable ledger names (§11) so the next run can compare mechanically. If a name no longer fits, retire it explicitly and say what replaced it. Tell apart a change that is **placement** (a file moved between areas, or the guide edited) from one that is **code** (an import added or removed): this window has a guide edit, so both kinds are live.
* **Run the review.** Do not re-derive the dependency numbers by searching. Run `scripts/code-shape/seams.mjs <repoDir> <commit> [areaGuidePath]` at HEAD and at `5334c81a7207b9f2cc85ca429a2c6b18e1635c0e` **with the same area guide for both runs**, so a difference is code that moved and not a map that was edited. Run both guides at both commits so the guide effect is recorded apart from code movement. Record the full commit you measured. The tool reports facts only: links between areas, knots (pairs of areas that import each other both ways, and the groups they form) and each area's entry files, plus counts of what it could not read, which you must report rather than ignore. Everything else is your judgement, written as prose with no scores and no clustering: *wrong-way dependencies* (for example run logic importing page renderers), *hub modules* that much of the code imports and that import much of it, *whether each area has a clear way in* (its entry files, and whether callers use them), *rebuild readiness per area* (could it be refactored or rebuilt behind a seam, and what stops it) and *where the areas the import graph suggests differ from the guide's names*. Report changes since the previous report first. The guide is a guide, not a rule: propose edits to it in the report, record guide edits separately from code movement, and add no test, check or count that enforces it. The finding-classes above are **examples, not a limit. Discover the complete set for this remit from the repo; a class list is a floor to build on, never a ceiling to stay inside.**
* **Read change coupling beside the import coupling.** Run `scripts/code-shape/cochange.mjs <repoDir> <commit> --areas <guide> --days 60` at HEAD and at `5334c81a…`, with the same area guide and the same window length for both runs, and report its top pairs beside the knots, with what moved between the two and against run 5 §6's figures. Report its counts of what it could not place (unmapped files, `shallow`) rather than ignore them. Say how much of the window the two runs share. Read a pair that changes together often yet has no link between its areas in `seams.mjs`'s output as a candidate seam: coupling the imports do not show, and a likely reason merges queue behind each other. State it as prose, with no score and nothing enforced. This is about pairs of areas only; per-file churn is the Stability Review's.
* **Mind the altitude. Do not double-flag.** This review reads the **direction and tangling between areas**. Decisions held in several places and the direction between individual files belong to the Drift & Coherence Review; function size belongs to the Code Quality Review; churn belongs to the Stability Review. Cross-link them where relevant; do not re-flag what they own.
* **Write an uncapped, trend-framed report** at `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-YYYY-MM-DD.md` (distinct name, see Grounding), evidence (raw JSON from every tool run, and byte copies of both guides) in `docs/reviews/_evidence-YYYY-MM-DD…/`. Confirm that convention before writing. If discovery genuinely turns up no such place, put the full report in a comment on this task instead of inventing a new location. The deliverable is a clear, severity-ranked report of everything found. Finding nothing, one thing or several are all valid; do not pad, cap or invent make-work. Ground each finding in the tool output at HEAD and the source it points to, not prior prose. Close with a compact trend ledger: each knot, hub and area under a stable, descriptive name, with its severity and its delta against the previous run, plus the change-coupling top pairs as rows with their run 5 values.
* **Mint a bounded set of follow-up tasks: highest-severity only.** Create at most the top \~3 by severity in Linear (fewer is fine; zero is valid when nothing rises to that bar, and in an 8-commit window it usually will). Each is well-scoped: a title, and a description that carries the problem, why it matters, acceptance and file anchors. A fix idea is allowed but goes under an "Unvalidated idea" heading, so later stages treat it as a hypothesis. Leave each in its default state. **Before minting, search for an existing ticket already naming the same finding** (LIN-4154, LIN-4155, LIN-4193, LIN-3922, LIN-3923, LIN-3736/3737/3738/3555/2600, LIN-4195 and its pieces). If one exists, note it in the report instead of minting a duplicate. Record EVERY finding in the report, including the ones not promoted. Err toward under-creating, and weigh whether a new ticket will be worked before minting it, and say why.
* **Shape each follow-up as one move.** Scope every minted task to a single move (for example invert a dependency, give an area one way in, or move a shared piece down a level) and the seam it would open. The move itself and where the code ends up go under its "Unvalidated idea" heading. Do not mint a task that untangles several areas at once. A guide edit is a guide proposal in the report, not a code move.
* **Get a fresh-context adversarial second-read before this task can conclude. This is a required, structural step, not advice.** After the report and any follow-up tasks are written, and before the Done transition, a genuinely separate reader must answer one question cold: *"what is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"* **Tier 1 (preferred):** a wholly separate session with no memory of this run. **Tier 2 (accepted fallback):** a fresh-context sub-agent carrying no memory of the report-writing turn. **Tier 3** (this same session re-reading its own report "from a cold stance") **is not accepted**; state which of Tier 1 or Tier 2 you used. Then post **one** comment on this task holding, together in a single body: `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`; `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO` (whether the reader's own answer differed from the report's top-ranked finding, independent of the verdict); and `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated` or `Disposition: no change`. The engine reads that comment and refuses Done until all three are present in one body. Copy the same three fields into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report, with the tier, the question and the reader's answer in full. **AGREE and DISAGREE both conclude this task normally. A DISAGREE verdict is itself the escalation**, never a reason to leave this task open.
* **Merge your own report PR.** This task owns it. Once its required CI checks (`ci-success`) are green, merge it before the Done transition. The report is docs-only, so merging it yourself is safe. Only when merging is genuinely impossible (no merge permission, required checks still red) may this task conclude with the PR open, and then only as an explicit handoff naming the blocker in the closing comment. An open report PR is not a normal terminal state.
* **Then conclude this task. Do not leave it open.** Post a concise, severity-ranked summary of the report as a comment on this task, with a link to the merged report (a GitHub commit, PR or blob URL, which the report gate needs). Then move this task to Done. A review task left open is re-recommended indefinitely; the follow-up tasks carry the actionable work forward.
* **Stay review-only.** Producing the report changes no code, config, guide or secrets, and no docs beyond the report artifact and its evidence. An operator instruction to avoid touching files is about the code and docs *under review*; it does not override this task's own deliverable.

## Run 6 research notes: grounding

Beat 1 of 5. Nothing has been written to the repo. Everything below was checked against git objects or Linear on 2026-11-04 at about 18:30Z.

### Measured SHA
- **HEAD = `d7ceb373444f9efbc027656132352d247535aa5e`** (origin/main after `git fetch`, committed 17:18:18Z). **Main has not moved since mint.**
- **Baseline = `5334c81a7207b9f2cc85ca429a2c6b18e1635c0e`** (05:23:59Z). It exists and is run 5's measured commit.
- **Window:** `git log --oneline 5334c81a..d7ceb373` lists **8 commits**: 4 are docs-only reports (`e439f637`, `1403d52d`, `57b22b92`, `f5bc752c`) and 4 are code (`230cc2c2` LIN-4200, `eb44eff9` LIN-4212, `2ee4e600` LIN-4201, `d7ceb373` LIN-4203).
- `git diff --shortstat 5334c81a d7ceb373 -- lib routes public server.js` → **33 files, +1,049 / −288**. Nothing under `public/` changed.
- `--name-status`: **A** `lib/request-usage-{fold,loader,vocabulary}.js`, `lib/usage-snapshot-intake.js`, `lib/workspace-kpis-cache.js`; **D** `lib/founder-lookup.js`.
- Scope file count: `git ls-tree` of `lib routes public server.js` (`.js/.mjs/.cjs`) gives **536 → 540**. The tool still has to confirm this.

### Mint-time claims: verified
- **`lib/` → `routes/` imports: 0 at both commits.** Checked with `git grep` for `../routes/` and `./routes/` import forms under `lib/`.
- **The guide edit, `2ee4e600`, is exactly two lines:**
  - `cost-read|row-usage|lineage-membership` was appended to the Runs `lib/(…)` alternation (`areas.json:24`).
  - `workspace-kpis-cache` was added to the Reports pattern (`areas.json:44`).
  - `git diff 5334c81a d7ceb373 -- scripts/code-shape/` touches only `areas.json`.
- **The tools did not change in the window.** `seams.mjs` and `cochange.mjs` were last touched by `b45aeff2` (LIN-3860). Their shared `code-shape-lib.mjs` was last touched by `856d8ae6` (LIN-3881), so the ticket's "last touched by LIN-3881" holds through the shared lib.
- **Catch-all arithmetic.** I re-implemented the guide's first-match over `git ls-tree`, with JS regex semantics, in a scratch script. It gives the same figures as the ticket:

  | code \ guide | old guide | HEAD guide |
  |---|---|---|
  | `5334c81a` | 17 | 14 |
  | `d7ceb373` | 17 | 14 |

- **Still catch-all at HEAD:** `key-state.js`, `key-state-holders.js` and `cost-format.js`.
- **`workspace-issues-memo.js` is still in Auth**, through `workspace-(?!kpi-stats\.js)[^/]*`.
- **The three `request-usage-*` files are in Runs** under both guides, by the LIN-4198 `request-usage-[^/]*` pattern.
- **Carried anchors are unchanged:**
  - `fmtDuration` is at `lib/render-run-steps.js:258`, imported by `task-state.js:22`, `task-page-loader.js:50` and `render-task-page.js:58`.
  - `applyDefaultDispatchHarness` is at `lib/proxy-preamble.js:152`.
  - The `tree.js:189` re-export from `recommendation-facts.js` is still there.
  - None of the 33 changed files is `proxy-wire`, `proxy-preamble`, `recap-cache`, `tree` or `recommendation-facts`.
- **F6 (browser globals) is unchanged:**
  - `window.X =` appears 100 times in `public/` and 52 times in `common.js` (48 with the stricter pattern), at both commits.
  - `/cost-format.js` is still in the same 6 renderer `scripts:` lists.
- **Raw importer-file counts are unchanged at both commits:** `proxy-preamble` 11, `tree` 8, `run-controls` 21, `task-page-loader` 8. These count all importers. Cross-area figures come from the tool next beat.
- **Route → route:** my `./x.js` import-line grep gives 55 at both commits. That is a different definition from run 5's 53. The delta is 0, and the tool's edge dump will give the comparable figure.
- **PR #2185 (LIN-4028) is still OPEN**, last updated 2026-10-30, and not on main. Its `lib/routing-ruling.js` would also land in the catch-all under the HEAD guide.
- **Simple Dispatcher is still flat CommonJS** at origin/main `d8d186c0`: `dispatcher.js` has 35 `require(` and 0 `import`/`export` lines, and `package.json` has no `"type"` field. It stays outside `seams.mjs`.

### Mint-time claims: refuted or incomplete
1. **"Other features 14 at both commits" is the right count, but the members are not the same.**
   - At `5334c81a` (HEAD guide), the 14 includes `founder-lookup.js`.
   - At `d7ceb373`, `founder-lookup.js` is gone and **`lib/usage-snapshot-intake.js`, new in the window, falls to the catch-all under both guides**.
   - So the window adds one new catch-all file that LIN-4201's guide edit did not name.
   - It imports nothing and has two importers: `lib/dispatch-store.js:59` (Runs → Other) and `server.js:42`.
2. **`workspace-kpis-cache.js` was not a catch-all file.** Under the old guide it lands in **Auth**, through the same over-broad `workspace-` pattern. The guide edit moved it Auth → Reports. That is a placement change outside the 17 → 14 arithmetic.
3. **LIN-3736 now has a parent (LIN-3449)**, and **LIN-2600 has parent LIN-2601**. The ticket lists both as unparented. LIN-3555, LIN-3737, LIN-3738 and LIN-3922 are unparented. All six are Backlog.
4. **N8 has partly moved:**
   - LIN-4203 removed the `runner.mjs:768` comment that cited `lib/task-cost.js`.
   - Two `lib/` comments remain: `model-routing-spend.js:5` and `wall-clock-summary.js:97`.
   - The dead `task-cost|` alias is still in the Runs pattern, on the very line LIN-4201 edited.
5. **Run 5's prediction for the store did not hold.** Run 5 expected `request-usage-store`'s importers to grow from 1 to about 7. **The store still has 1 importer** (`request-usage-intake.js:29`). The new door is **`lib/request-usage-loader.js`**:
   - It has 6 production importers: `model-routing-history` (LLM), `run-paragraph-hook` (Runs), `workspace-kpi-stats` (Reports), `routes/dashboard-effort` and `routes/dashboard` (Web routes), and `routes/proxy-compute` (Agent API).
   - It is built once at `server.js:136` and injected. Its only import is `lineage-membership.js`.
6. **N6 (`cost-read`) is mostly placement, with a small code change.**
   - **Code:** +1 import (`request-usage-fold`, intra-Runs), and the file grew from 434 to 592 lines. It has the same 9 importer files as run 5.
   - **Placement:** with `cost-read` now in Runs, 4 of those 9 are intra-area (`effort-readout`, `run-view`, `terminal-marked-task-cost`, `weekly-budget`). That leaves 5 cross-area importers from 4 areas: LLM (`model-routing-spend`), Reports (`workspace-kpi-stats`), Agent API (`proxy-compute`) and Web routes (`settings`, `ship-biscuit`).
   - Its cross-area outbound edges are `llm-call-log` (LLM) and `utils/time` (Platform).
   - The tool confirms this next beat.

### LIN-4193: run 5's comment was posted
- Run 5's comment was posted on LIN-4193 at 08:07Z, with a correction at 08:25Z.
